opening_message:
Ticket 1: Kim Dunn (employee ID E048) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 6 note(s) about employee E048.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: admin
  - comment: Kim Dunn (E048) is a full-time Engineer requesting admin access to Source Code. As a full-time employee whose role owns the Source Code system, admin is permitted per policy.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by IT agent:
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: full_time (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - recommendation for Source Code: admin
  - comment: IT DB confirms Kim Dunn (E048) has role Engineer. HR confirms full-time employment. Per policy, full-time employees may receive admin only if their role owns the system; Engineer owns Source Code, so admin is permitted. Recommend granting admin (requested level).
Note 3 (ticket 1), written by Finance agent:
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent, note 2 by IT agent)
  - employment type: full_time (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent, note 2 by IT agent)
  - recommendation for Source Code: admin
  - comment: Finance DB confirms Kim Dunn (E048) has role Engineer. HR confirms full-time employment. As a full-time Engineer whose role owns Source Code, admin is permitted per policy. Requested admin is at the allowed maximum, so recommend granting admin.
Note 4 (ticket 1), written by Compliance agent:
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent, note 2 by IT agent, note 3 by Finance agent)
  - employment type: full_time (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent, note 2 by IT agent, note 3 by Finance agent)
  - recommendation for Source Code: admin
  - comment: Compliance DB confirms Kim Dunn (E048) has role Engineer. HR confirms full-time employment. As a full-time Engineer, the role owns Source Code, so admin is permitted per policy. Requested admin equals the allowed maximum; recommend granting admin.
Note 5 (ticket 1), written by Facilities agent:
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent, note 2 by IT agent, note 3 by Finance agent, note 4 by Compliance agent)
  - employment type: full_time (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent, note 2 by IT agent, note 3 by Finance agent, note 4 by Compliance agent)
  - recommendation for Source Code: admin
  - comment: Facilities DB confirms Kim Dunn (E048) has role Engineer. HR confirms full-time employment. As a full-time Engineer whose role owns Source Code, admin is permitted per policy. Requested admin equals the allowed maximum, so recommend granting admin.
Note 6 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Engineer (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent, note 2 by IT agent, note 3 by Finance agent, note 4 by Compliance agent, note 5 by Facilities agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Kim Dunn (E048) is a contractor with basic security training. Per policy, contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training, and never admin. The requested admin exceeds the maximum, so the maximum allowed level is read. Recommend granting read.
reason: Request: Kim Dunn (E048) requests admin to Source Code. Most notes rely on HR's claim of full-time employment without verifying it themselves, but the Security agent independently looked up E048 in their own database and found the employee is a contractor with basic security training. Per policy, contractors may have read, or write only with advanced security training, and never admin. Since admin is above the maximum allowable level for a contractor with basic training, the maximum allowed level is read. Never granting more than requested, the decision is read.

2. contractor employees: read, or write if they have advanced security training. Never admin.

The other agents relied on HR for employment type (they didn't look it up in their own databases). HR looked up employment type in their own database and said full_time.

So there's a conflict: HR says full_time, Security says contractor.
